mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, وَهُوَ بالأفق الْأَعْلَى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in استوى, i.e. "he rose, being high", meaning Gabriel, upon him be peace; so the two pronouns are for Gabriel.
Al-Farrāʾ said it [هو] is conjoined to the pronoun in استوى: he made the pronoun in استوى refer to Muhammad ﷺ and هو the pronoun of Gabriel, upon him be peace, conjoining to the nominative latent pronoun without its being emphasised, and that is ugly according to the Basrans. Had the verse been taken in this sense, the regular form according to them would be to say فاستوى هو وهو ("so he rose, he and he") at the horizon. استوى applies to one, and most often it applies to two; for that reason al-Farrāʾ made the two pronouns refer to two persons.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying أَو أدنى: أو is in its basic sense, and the meaning is: had one of you seen him, he would have said: he is the length of two bows or nearer, in closeness.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying مَا كذب الْفُؤَاد مَا رأى: whoever reads كَذَبَ without doubling makes ما in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition (accusative by removal of the preposition), i.e. "in what it saw" (فيما رأى), with ما meaning الذي, and رأى falling upon an omitted هاء, i.e. رآه; and رأى is from seeing with the eye. It is also possible that ما with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so there is no need to imply a هاء. Whoever reads كذّب with doubling makes ما a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), on either of the two interpretations, and the omission of a preposition is not assumed in it, because when the verb is doubled it becomes transitive without a particle.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying نزلة أُخْرَى: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as if He said "and he certainly saw him descending another descent" (ولقد رآه نازلا نزلة أخرى). According to al-Farrāʾ it is accusative because it is in the position of an adverb, since its meaning is "another time" (مرة أخرى). And the هاء in رآه refers back to Gabriel, upon him be peace.
His saying وما لهم بِهِ من علم: the هاء refers back to الأسماء (the names), because التسمية (naming) and الأسماء have the same meaning.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying وَكم من ملك: كم is the khabariyya (declarative) [كم], and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لا تغني is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying هُوَ أعلم بِمن ضل: أعلم means عالم (knowing); like it is وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى. There is room for reservation in this, because أفعل only has the meaning of فاعل when it is used by one speaking about himself. It is also possible that both are in their basic sense of preference in knowledge, i.e. He knows these two kinds, and others, better than anyone. Like that is هو أعلم بكم and هو أعلم بمن اتقى.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying ليجزي الَّذين: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning, because the meaning of ولله ما في السموات وما في الأرض is "He is the Owner of all; He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, in order to recompense". It is also said that the lām is attached to His saying لا تغني شفاعتهم.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying الَّذين يجتنبون: الذين is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of الذين in His saying ويجزي الذين أحسنوا.
His saying إِلَّا اللمم: an exception not of the same kind as the first (disconnected exception), and it [اللمم] is the minor sins, from their saying ألممت بالشيء إلماما ("I touched upon the thing") when you take little of it, and زرت لماما, i.e. "I visited rarely". This is the best of the views about it.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying أَلا تزر: أن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of ما in His saying لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى, or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is: that no bearer bears" (ذلك ألا تزر). The هاء is omitted with أن, i.e. "that it is that no bearer bears" (أنه لا تزر).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying وَأَن لَيْسَ للإنسان and وَأَن سَعْيه: أن in both places is conjoined to ألا تزر. Al-Zajjāj permitted سوف يَرى with a fatḥa on the yāʾ on the assumption of an implied هاء, i.e. "he will see it" (سوف يراه); the Kufans did not permit it, because سعيه would then be governed by both أن and يرى. It is permissible according to al-Mubarrad and others, because the entry of أن upon سعيه and its governing it indicate the هاء omitted from يرى. On this basis the Basrans permitted إن زيدا ضربت ("Zayd, I struck") without a هاء.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying ثمَّ يجزاه: the هاء refers back to السعي, i.e. he will be recompensed for it; and الجزاء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying وَأَن إِلَى رَبك, وَأَنه هُوَ أضْحك, وَأَنه هُوَ أمات, وَأَنه خلق: أن in all of that is conjoined to ألا تزر on one of its two interpretations, and likewise أن in what comes after that.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t:
His saying عادا الأولى: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr assimilated the tanwīn into the lām of الأولى, after transferring the vowel of the ḍamma-vowelled hamza of أولى onto the lām of definition. Al-Mubarrad and others rejected that, because the two of them assimilated a quiescent letter into one whose origin is quiescence and whose vowel is accidental, and the accidental is not taken into account.
The justification of their reading with assimilation is what al-Māzinī and others related of the speech of the Arabs: لَحْمَر جاء ("the red one came"), meaning الأحمر; they took the vowel of the lām into account, began with it, and dispensed through it with the connective alif (alif al-waṣl). Likewise whoever assimilates the tanwīn of عاد into the lām of الأولى takes into account the vowel on the lām. On that basis they said سَلْ زيدا, which is really اسأل: when the vowel of the hamza was transferred onto the سين, it was taken into account and the connective alif was omitted. On that basis they said رُدَّ, عَضَّ and مُدَّ, whose origin is افْعَل; then the vowel of the second radical (ʿayn) was transferred onto the first radical (fāʾ), and they took it into account and omitted the connective alif because they took into account the vowel of the fāʾ, even though it was accidental.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying والمؤتفكة: accusative by أهوى.
